title: [Mask Accessibility A1] Derive accessible controls from Face and certified component contracts
body:
Parent: #5354. Depends on semantic baseline #5355 and separation contract #5364; consumes structural recipes #5365 and theme packages #5366. Accepted precedent #2875 rendered accessibility proof and #4133 Face semantic names.

## Outcome
Move accessibility semantics and interactive control behavior into a **trusted, checked compiler/lowering path**. App authors can create rich visual components and themes, but certified components cannot supply a bogus role/ARIA label, unbound click action, inaccessible keyboard trap or brand-specific contradictory state. Meaning must be authored in Face before it can be visually realized.

## Model
```text
Validated Face + checked component recipe
      |                 |
      +--> generated semantic/accessibility traversal
      +--> bounded visual composition (styled with ThemePack)
                    |
       correspondence + rendering checks
                    |
         platform realization / Show
```
A theme never supplies accessible names, statuses, widget roles or action identities; these are derived from Face and typed component intent. A component cannot claim `checkbox` for a one-way `complete` action absent a reversible state contract. Native HTML elements preferred in browser; ARIA is emitted by the trusted backend only where needed, with matching keyboard and state behavior. Native/linear/speech paths preserve meanings and offer accurate limitations, not a fictitious OS accessibility service.

## Required checks
- Semantic completeness: all required Face subjects, names, status, actions, available/unavailable/refused states and meaningful order/disclosure have a reachable valid representation or a declared equivalent/fallback. *Presentation* can emphasize/deemphasize but cannot erase required agency.
- Control correctness: role/state/input contract compatible with actual typed Face affordance; no author-supplied arbitrary `aria-*`, `role`, `tabindex`, event callback or interactive hit geometry overrides in certified component/theme DSL. The Host owns native keyboard/pointer mechanics, focus routing and Show-bound `FaceInteraction`.
- Visual/accessibility correspondence: if decorative overlay, zoom, high contrast, reduced motion, reflow or animation obscures a required control or makes it unreachable, fail rendering or select verified safe fallback. A merely well-formed ARIA tree is insufficient.
- Timing: stale source Face/Show/Host and updates preserve/refuse with explicit focus migration, no invisible action on old DOM/scene. Model-assisted graphical proposals pass through same compiler, never privileged.
- Raw external HTML/CSS/JS can exist only via an explicitly **uncertified** external Host/capability path with a truthful label and generic accessible fallback; don't promise static proof over arbitrary code.
- Negative fixtures: mismatched role (button vs checkbox), missing accessible name, color-only status, CSS `display:none`, focus-reordered layout, overlapping pointer blocker, missing action argument, stale Show, provider output trying to insert role/action, loss/cancellation/pressure.
- Incorporate axe/Playwright WCAG 2.2 AA structural audits where appropriate and manual assistive-tech tests as separately recorded human evidence. Don't claim complete accessibility mathematically or infer it from zero automated scanner violations.

## Acceptance
- [ ] Two distinct visual themes and two components produce truthful accessible names/roles/states and correct keyboard/pointer behavior from the same underlying Face.
- [ ] Deliberately invalid component or theme code **cannot enter the certified renderer** and produces a typed refusal or accessible fallback; no custom ARIA exposed to app authors in that certified language.
- [ ] Identical semantic actions across browser/native/terminal/spoken Masks with context/Show/revision correlation; no hidden alternate action route.
- [ ] Automated structural, runtime keyboard/focus, contrast/reflow, forced-colors/reduced-motion, missing capability, stale/lost Host and malicious proposal tests pass.
- [ ] Fallback is fully usable when no custom component/theme or model is installed; exact Show acknowledgement and proof class remains honest.
- [ ] Native target accessibility claims match actual available interfaces; limitations and human testing are recorded separately.

## Ownership
Trusted semantic/accessibility lowering near `semantics/presentation`, browser host `targets/browser/host/assets/application-presentation.mjs` mapping, native `targets/conduitos/src/native_face_scene/` linkage and existing conformance tests. Coordinate with F2/F3 to avoid competing modifications.

## Stop line
This is a certified safe path, **not** a claim that unrestricted CSS/JavaScript/HTML or subjective usability can be proven correct. Do not shift semantic authority to components, themes, ARIA attributes, LLM output, or a browser-only component model. Complete richer component certification may land after first playable Commons; architecture guardrails apply to F3 immediately.

## Look and physical-button regression (2026-10-09)
Apply the canonical **Look** contract #5368: a Look may style visible controls, prosody and generative expression but never supplies accessible names, authoritative wording/action, control-role semantics, focus order, input binding or a bogus alternative ARIA tree. Component authoring is **Fore-first** as ordinary checked Plots (#5365), not a separate widget authority. Add #5369 Parsec-like acceptance: one `game/start` Face action, a current Fire-controller mapping, visual arcade prompt plus optional voiced prompt from the same accepted action/binding; after remapping the device, update both accurately without changing Look or action identity. A virtual graphical button is one possible presentation of `activate`, not a semantic `Button` Kind. An unimplemented physical speech/back must never be claimed available merely because the Look requests an announcer.


## Certified Web Component and CSS correspondence proof
#5376 makes one presentation Gear's browser Back a registered, actual Web Component. #5379 adds real scoped CSS, not merely a color-token object. Treat shadow/light DOM and CSS **as effects to be checked**, not a second application semantics API. The selected Face/Fore and current Show supply names/states/typed actions. The trusted Host supplies browser-native controls, focus and appropriate accessibility representation. CSS may use flexible geometry and density reflow, but attempts to conceal, reorder semantically important content, block hit/focus, replace required wording or forge a control must refuse/fallback. Static CSS syntax filtering alone cannot prove WCAG or subjective usability; test actual Chromium runtime at narrow viewports, zoom, keyboard traversal and forced colors. Arbitrary untrusted component JavaScript is not a certified route merely because it uses Custom Elements. #5380 provides separate spoken traversal for the same Face.

---

## Thin delivery slices (2026-10-13)
- [ ] **A1** #5630: Derive semantic names, roles and actions from exact Face and component Fores
- [ ] **A2** #5631: Certify keyboard/focus interactions and stale action refusal
- [ ] **A3** #5632: Prove hostile styling cannot conceal mandatory accessible controls

Depends on source Face #5355 and structured components #5365; controls and accessibility names must be derived from trusted semantics.

Queued, not automatically active; coordinate Look/Mask files under #5520 WIP limit.
